Free.
Works through WhatsApp.
You can literally send it a voice note like you would to an employee, and it starts working on the task.

It’s called Instinct, and I’ve been playing with it for the last few days.

There’s almost nothing new to learn.

You text it, send a voice note, or talk to it and tell it what you want done.

It can research, browse websites, use accounts you connect, contact people and businesses, make bookings and purchases, follow up, and keep working on a task over time.

Your Instinct can now talk directly to someone else’s Instinct.

I can send my AI assistant to coordinate a meeting with your AI assistant, and let them figure it out between them.

summary: Claude skills build repeatable AI employees
html:
Good once is luck.

Good every time is a skill.

And a skill is much more than a saved prompt.

A skill is a complete way of doing a job, written for Claude.

The steps.
The decisions.
The checks.
The standard for what “good” looks like.

Once Claude has that, you don’t need to explain the job from scratch every time.

Same process.
Same standards.
Different product.

That is how I built Wonka, my AI creative employee.

Instead of one giant prompt, Wonka has individual skills for the jobs I want him to know how to do.

For example:

🔬 /meet-my-product
He researches the niche, customer reviews and competitors before the creative work even starts.

🧠 /creative-brief
He maps out what every image in the listing needs to communicate before generating anything.

🔎 /inspect
He checks every image at Amazon thumbnail size and catches things that looked great full screen but disappear when a customer sees them on a phone.

And one of my favorites:

🍫 /tasting-room
It builds a synthetic panel of around 100 AI shoppers modeled on the target buyer demographics.

Then your new creative races against the image already live on Amazon.

A new image doesn’t win because Wonka likes it.

It has to beat what you already have.

And every AI taster explains why they chose what they chose. Those objections become inputs for the next improvement.

These are AI shoppers, not real people. But having a structured way to challenge creative before putting it live is incredibly useful.

During the Wonka Creative Bootcamp, we install 15 skills covering the process from product research through creative planning, generation, inspection, testing and improvement.

And they don’t disappear when the bootcamp ends. They stay installed in your Wonka for the next product too.

That is the part of Claude Code I find so interesting.

A prompt tells AI what to do this time.

A skill teaches your AI employee how the job gets done.

Jay

summary: Anthropic launches Claude updates and limits
html:
Anthropic shipped a lot this week. Let me sort it out for you.

1. Fable 5 is now a permanent part of the plans
For weeks Anthropic kept me on edge about Fable 5. Every few days they extended access a little more, with no way to know if the model was staying or disappearing. I stayed up at night just to use it before the window closed.
Now we finally have certainty. It stays as a permanent part of Max and Team Premium seats, at up to 50% of the weekly limit.
Heads up: this is not an extra 50% on top of your limit. It is the option to spend up to half of your existing weekly limit on Fable.
On Pro and Team Standard the model is still available, but through paid usage credits. If you were subscribed before July 19 you get a one-time $100 credit, and you need to activate it in settings by August 2. Don't miss it.

2. Claude Code weekly limits went up 50%
Through August 19, all Pro, Max, and Team users get 50% more weekly usage in Claude Code. Hit your ceiling mid-task? You have a lot more room now. Nothing to do, it is already live.

3. The Team plan now starts at 2 users
Until this week you needed at least 5. Now you can open a Team plan with just two. For a small team or partners who work together regularly, it suddenly became a much more accessible option, with more usage than Pro.

4. Claude Code got a built-in browser
Inside the desktop app, Claude Code can now open documentation, designs, and websites in its own browser window. It reads the page, clicks buttons, and checks the site, all in an isolated environment, without touching your Chrome or your personal tabs.
And you stay in control: you decide whether to keep the browsing data or wipe it completely.

At the pace Anthropic is moving, another update probably dropped before you finished reading this. 😅

Hit 👍 if you are a little addicted to Claude too.
